text:
eva: Heads-up — saw a recurring pattern in metrics: many dashboard panel queries within a 100ms window are identical for org-scoped views. Spiking DB/query-layer load and SLO breaches. Thinking: add a lightweight coalescer at the console query service to collapse identical queries for short windows and return the same result to multiple callers. Open to tradeoffs.

sam: Can you paste the sample traces? curious about cardinality of "identical" requests. :eyes:

eva: paste logs:```
2026-03-18T14:12:05Z GET /console/query?panel=recent-usage&org=acme user=alice req_id=abc123
2026-03-18T14:12:05Z GET /console/query?panel=recent-usage&org=acme user=bob req_id=abc124
2026-03-18T14:12:05Z GET /console/query?panel=recent-usage&org=acme user=carol req_id=abc125
```
All three hit in ~8ms. backend work identical except auth scope.

mohit: Quick thought: RBAC is the tricky bit. naive coalescing that ignores per-user perms will leak. we need to either coalesce by permission-fingerprint or by org+role bucket.

eva: agreed. proposing coalesce key = hash(query_text + org_id + permission_fingerprint). permission_fingerprint = bitset of granted routes for the user (cached).

marco: How expensive is creating the fingerprint per request? if it's a DB lookup we lose the benefit.

mohit: we can compute fingerprint from cached token claims (JWT) or from a short LRU of recent users per org. should be O(1) in the common case.

iris: product note: some panels are user-personalized (e.g., "my tasks") and must never be coalesced across users. We'll need an allowlist or annotation on dashboard panels that opt out.

eva: yep. default: coalesce enabled for org-scoped, not for user-scoped. panel-level config: coalesce: { mode: "auto|off|strict" }

sam: tradeoff: coalescing reduces QPS but introduces added latency up to the coalesce window. If window=50ms and no hit, tail latency increases. We need adaptive windowing. maybe target a latency budget: if p95 < SLO-10ms, we can use 50ms, else 10ms.

mohit: alternative: async-subscribe model — first request triggers backend call, others get an in-flight promise rather than waiting an explicit window. that's essentially de-duplication rather than time-window coalescing. cheaper tail effect.

eva: good point. implementation plan: in-flight dedupe + tiny buffer window (10ms) to capture near-simultaneous arrival from multiple frontend workers. config knobs: max_wait_ms, max_fanout, key_sharding.

natalie: SRE concern: we must be able to see per-caller metrics even when coalesced for billing/audit. Ensure logs include exploded copies or at least a join table in tracing: coalesced_key -> [req_ids]. Also make sure health-check/real-time panels bypass this.

eva: agreed. we will emit metric: coalesced_requests_total and histogram of fanout_size. traces include parent req and list of members.

marco: perf note: kernel — if backend response sizes vary a lot, fanout-based caching could amplify memory spikes. limit max_fanout and reject with fast-path when >N.

sam: also think about cache key granularity: query params canonicalization is painful. We should normalize queries (sort keys, trim insignificant params) at perimeter. failing that, add a deterministic canonicalizer so semantically-equal queries hit same key.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: eng-platform/coalescer-prototype -> staging in 15m :rocket:

iris: timeline question — how do we roll this out? canary by org size?
eva: rollout plan in brief: 1) feature flag + panel allowlist, 2) staging canary for low-traffic orgs, 3) enable in prod orgs < 100DAU for 24h, monitor SLOs and fanout metrics, 4) expand to medium orgs, 5) opt-in for large orgs while we tune.

mohit: follow-ups: add unit test for permission_fingerprint collisions, a load-test scenario with synthetic near-simultaneous calls, and integra test for trace join correctness.

natalie: add alert: if coalescer_fallback_rate > 1% (meaning we rejected coalescing due to max_fanout or error), fire P0 to eng-platform.

eva: action items: @sam to sketch API for canonicalizer + config flags, @mohit to prototype in-flight dedupe library, @natalie to write SLO/alert, @iris to create panel allowlist rules, @marco to run memory fanout bench. I'll own the canary rollout doc.

sam: I'll put up a short RFC follow-up doc in docs/eng-platform tomorrow.

eva: thanks all. tagging this resolved for now — we'll track in the RFC thread. :thumbsup:
